description: Language-neutral parity catalog for `plainkeep __complete` (bin/lib/completion.py + bin/__complete/run.py <-> cli/src/core/complete.ts, registered in dispatch.ts INTERCEPTS). Every case runs the SAME argv through the compiled binary (which answers it in-process) and through the bash floor (which spawns the real Python verb), byte-comparing exit code, stdout, stderr AND the gate's audit line. That audit-line comparison is what proves the interception is POST-GATE: an interception placed before the gate would leave the core side's .logs empty and every case here would fail on 'log presence differs'. Fixture grammar additions over guardrail.json (additive): engine_from_repo installs REAL bin/<verb>/ dirs plus the whole bin/lib/ from the repo, so the reference side runs the actual completion brain rather than a restatement of it; vault_files writes vault-relative plain files, which is what the completion PROVIDERS read. Invocation additions: expect_stdout asserts BOTH sides' stdout byte-exactly (the only way to assert an output is EMPTY), and expect_stdout_excludes asserts an absence on both sides — the latter is REFUSED unless the same invocation carries a non-empty positive assertion, because empty stdout satisfies every exclusion and would hide the exact failure the exclusion exists to catch. Invocation shape: {compare:'dispatch', verb:'__complete', args?:[...]}. Two kinds of case, matching the implemented split: TS-ANSWERS (the verb list, actions[], enums, and the many empty answers — all derivable from the cmd.json surface alone) and FALL-THROUGH (every arg whose candidates come from a live-vault provider), the latter proving the fall-through spawns the Python verb with the same argv and vault and so changes a provider case in no way.

cases.name: verb-surface
cases.rationale: The verb list: live from the cmd.json sidecars across engine + plugin packs, hidden verbs filtered, sorted by CODE POINT. Plus every branch that answers nothing at the verb slot — unknown verb, hidden verb, scalar verb — each asserted EMPTY rather than merely equal, so two sides wrong together cannot pass.

invocations.why: no prior words — the WHOLE surface, asserted byte-exactly: every visible verb with its summary, engine and plugin alike, in code-point order, and nothing else
invocations.expect_stdout:
compound:a compound verb
packverb:from a pack
scalar:a scalar verb
:pua
😀:astral

invocations.why: hidden verbs are filtered exactly as manifest.load_cmds() filters them. Asserted on BOTH sides and PAIRED with a verb that must be present: an empty stdout would satisfy the exclusion on its own and go green in the failure it exists to catch
a plugin pack's verb is part of the completion surface (the resolver is the one source for both sides)
sorted(cmds) is Python's CODE-POINT order: U+E000 precedes U+1F600, which JS's default UTF-16-unit sort reverses (field-guide item 2)
`plainkeep help <TAB>` completes to the same verb list — grammar, even though `help` ITSELF is not intercepted (run.md D6)
invocations.expect_stdout:
compound:a compound verb
packverb:from a pack
scalar:a scalar verb
:pua
😀:astral

invocations.why: `help` ignores anything already typed after it and still offers the verb list
an unknown verb answers nothing at all
a HIDDEN verb is unknown to completion even though it exists on disk (the guardrail still gates it)
a scalar verb (no actions[]) has no subaction grammar — nothing, not an error
...and nothing after it either, however many words are typed

cases.name: action-grammar
cases.rationale: Every branch of the walk that decides WHICH action and WHICH arg the next word fills: keyworded actions, the tokenless default action, inline enums, the value-flag/positional accounting of _walk, and positional exhaustion. Each empty answer is asserted EMPTY, not merely equal.

invocations.why: slot 1 of a compound verb: every keyworded action with its summary, and nothing else
slot 1 with a TOKENLESS default action: the keyworded actions PLUS the default action's first positional's values, with the default's own name NOT offered
first positional of a keyworded action, declaring neither enum nor provider — nothing
one positional consumed, so the NEXT positional's inline enum is offered
positionals exhausted — nothing
a value-flag as the LAST token: the next word is its VALUE, so its enum is offered rather than a positional's
a value-flag plus its value consumes NO positional, so the first positional is still the one being filled
...and the positional after it is reached normally once one is typed
a `type: flag` flag swallows nothing — it is skipped and the positional count is unchanged
an unrecognized `--flag` is skipped like any other dash token
an action with an empty args[] offers nothing, whatever follows it
a word that is no action name routes to the DEFAULT action and is consumed as its first positional
the default action's own NAME is not a keyword either — it is consumed as the first positional too
a value-flag before any positional on the default action: its value is consumed, so the first positional's enum is what comes next
a verb with actions[] but no default action, given a word that names none of them — nothing

cases.name: providers-fall-through
cases.rationale: The other half of the split: every arg whose candidates come from a live-vault PROVIDER falls through to the Python verb. Fixture content is deliberately ORDER-REVEALING — mixed case, digit prefixes, hyphens, and statuses/folders whose provider order is NOT alphabetical — so each expectation pins the ordering that a future in-core port of a provider would be most likely to get wrong (JS sort vs Python sort, alphabetical vs declared order). Outputs are small enough to assert byte-exactly, which also pins each provider's DESCRIPTION column and the narrowness of asset-slug.

invocations.why: note-slug — every wiki note, described by its frontmatter `type`, ordered by FULL PATH: directories alphabetically, then uppercase before lowercase ('Acme-Corp' < 'acme-2'), and lexicographic-not-numeric within a name ('apollo-11' < 'apollo-9'). Names never differ by CASE ALONE: this repo's macOS filesystem is case-insensitive, so 'Apple-Pie.md' and 'apple-pie.md' would silently be ONE file

invocations.why: note-type — the notetype registry (built-in defaults here, no templates/wiki/types.json), sorted, hub types described `hub` and the rest by their directory. Asserted as an ordered SLICE rather than exactly, so adding a built-in type does not falsely redden this case
task-id — statuses in filing's DECLARED order (active, waiting, inbox, done), NOT alphabetically, each sorted by name; the done task has no heading, so title_of falls back to the stem

invocations.why: status — filing.STATUSES in declared order, and the one provider whose rows carry NO description, so every line is a bare value with no colon at all

asset-slug — the NARROW wiki/files/ subset described by frontmatter `title`, proven narrow by the exact assertion (no ordinary note appears); its title carries a colon, so _clean is exercised through the fall-through

hub — clients, then projects, then areas: the DECLARED folder order, which alphabetical order would reverse. Reached as a SECOND positional, so the walk decides the arg before the provider is consulted

layer — a declared provider whose Python implementation returns nothing. It still falls through: the boundary is `does a provider decide this`, not `is this provider empty today`. NOTE this case cannot tell which side answered (both print nothing); the routing is pinned by complete.test.ts's all-seven-providers test
a `complete` naming something that is NOT in the provider set is not a provider at all — Python answers nothing and so does the in-core path

cases.name: sidecar-shapes
cases.rationale: The cmd.json shapes where a port could silently diverge from manifest.load_cmds() / _clean: Python truthiness vs JS truthiness for `hidden`, Python's str.strip() set vs JS trim()'s, the verb FIELD vs the directory name, a non-object sidecar, an empty actions[], and both directions of the empty-output boundary.

cmd.summary: its one action has an empty name

invocations.why: the whole surface at once, byte-exact: it pins _clean (every colon becomes ' -', then a PYTHON strip — this summary ends in \x1c, whitespace to str.strip() and NOT to JS trim()), Python-truthy `hidden` (bool([]) is False where Boolean([]) is true, so falsyhidden stays VISIBLE), an explicit hidden:false, the verb FIELD winning over the directory name, and the non-object sidecar being dropped
invocations.expect_stdout:
blank:its one action has an empty name
colons:a - b -c
emptyactions:actions is an empty list
explicitlyvisible:hidden is false
falsyhidden:hidden is an empty list
renamed:the field, not the directory

invocations.why: the non-object-sidecar drop, stated as its own named case so a failure says WHICH property broke — paired with a verb that must be present, since an empty surface would satisfy the exclusion by itself
the directory name never reaches the surface when the sidecar declares a different verb — same pairing rule
an EMPTY actions[] takes the same branch as no actions[] at all — nothing, not an empty action list
the empty-output boundary, asserted EXACTLY: ONE candidate whose value and description are both empty prints exactly one blank line and nothing else
the same boundary from the other side: no candidates prints NOTHING — not a blank line, not a trailing newline. Only an exact assertion can state this, since every string contains ""
